panels.title: Lab token
panels.description: The lab connection token and the collector's health. Blue when enrollment is open: a joining host redeems the 6-character code (pwsh test/lab/Set-LabToken.ps1 -LabToken CODE); the code is select-and-copy text -- there is no need to retype it. It omits i, l, o, 0 and 1, and a code you have just read stays valid for about three minutes, so there is no need to rush it. Red when the collector behind this dashboard has stopped: every panel may be stale. Gray when the token exchange is off. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Hosts total
panels.description: Distinct pool hosts seen within the aggregator's host TTL (24h by default, -host-ttl), keyed on the stable hostId (reachable or not). Driven by yuruna_pool_hosts_total from the pool-aggregator-service. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Success%
panels.description: Share of terminal cycles lab-wide that passed, within the selected time range (top-right). Includes historical cycles from hosts no longer in the live table. Shows 'n/a' when no cycle finished in range -- deliberately not 100%, so an idle pool cannot look healthy. Red below 95%, amber below 100%, green at 100%. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

targets.expr: 100 * ((sum(count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus="pass" [$__range])) or (sum(count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus=~"pass|fail" [$__range])) * 0)) / sum(count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus=~"pass|fail" [$__range])))

panels.title: Failed cycles
panels.description: Cycles that finished 'fail' across the whole LAB within the dashboard's selected time range (top-right), including hosts no longer in the live table. Counted from the Loki transition log (exact; reaches back to Loki retention, unlike a Prometheus counter window). Green when zero; red when any. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Total cycles
panels.description: Terminal cycles lab-wide within the selected time range, including hosts no longer in the live table; also the denominator behind Success%. A still-running cycle has no terminal status and is not counted. The dashboard is lab-wide -- per-pool figures live on the pool-control board. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Addresses in use
panels.description: MEASURED count of IPv4 addresses the lab holds now: the proxy's observed clients plus registered hosts' addresses, deduplicated. A FLOOR, not a ceiling -- whatever is invisible to both sources is not counted. It says nothing about the DHCP pool: scope size and free leases live on the DHCP server; read those before concluding exhaustion. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Extension hosts
panels.description: Hosts self-reporting an extension function (e.g. stash, pool-control, download-agent) -- the same Host ID namespace as Pool hosts. The Extension link opens that service's UI, already unlocked unless the proxy mints no token. Extension-only hosts have no status page: open hosts from the Pool hosts table instead. Click a Host ID for its full GUID form. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Pool hosts
panels.description: One row per discovered host, named only by its opaque Host ID -- hostname-free, safe to expose unauthenticated. Pass and Fail combine cycles from this ID and any prior ID handed over to it within the selected time range. Yellow preflight failures are runner attempts, excluded from cycle counts. Watch Status first: 'runner stopped' means the results below are a record, not a live reading. Control says whether the host link will let you drive the host ('remote' works; 'onsite' will 403); the link always opens read-only. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

targets.expr: topk(1, yuruna_pool_host_info{pool=~".+"}) by (hostId) unless on(hostId) yuruna_pool_host_retired
sum by (hostId) (count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus="pass" [$__range])) or (sum by (hostId) (count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus=~"pass|fail" [$__range])) * 0)
sum by (hostId) (count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus="fail" [$__range])) or (sum by (hostId) (count_over_time({pool=~".+"} | json | overallStatus=~"pass|fail" [$__range])) * 0)

panels.title: Host state over time (host x UTC time)
panels.description: One row per host, one color per observed host state; times are UTC. Yellow preflight failures happen before a cycle starts and do not count as failed cycles. Red means a test cycle or another runner failure. Open results or diagnostics to inspect the matching attempt or cycle; share applies to cycles. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

links.title: Open results or diagnostics for this host at this time

panels.title: Incidents (open / resolved)
panels.description: Incident lifecycle: a host opens an incident at N or more failed cycles within a trailing window (default 3 in 2h) and resolves once the window clears. Each line carries the incident's failure class; a cross-host incident requires the same class on every host. From the aggregator's incident correlation (src=incident in Loki). Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Failures by class & severity (window)
panels.description: The failure-class histogram: step_failure events over the dashboard time range, grouped by failureClass + severity. Driven by the per-step NDJSON tailed into Loki (src=event, event=step_failure). Click a failure class for its meaning and first checks. Sorted by count -- the dominant failure modes across the pool. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

targets.expr: sum by (failureClass, severity) (count_over_time({pool=~"$pool", src="event"} | json | event="step_failure" [$__range]))

panels.title: Recent step failures across the pool (which step failed)
panels.description: step_failure events tailed from each host's per-cycle NDJSON: the failing step's action, number, failure class, severity and reason, per host/cycle. Expand a line for full detail; the table's deep-links open that host's full cycle artifacts. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Cycle event stream across the pool (all steps)
panels.description: Every per-cycle NDJSON event (cycle_start / step_end / step_failure / typed sub-events) tailed from each host. Use the Grafana log search to filter, e.g. cycleStartUtc=... or event=step_end. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Cycle status transitions across the pool (24h)
panels.description: One line each time a host's cycle changes state (running -> pass/fail), from the status.json poll: hostId, cycleStartUtc, overallStatus and a baseUrl for drill-down. The cycle-level audit trail behind the table and timeline above. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Incidents by failure class (window)
panels.description: Per-host incidents over the dashboard time range, grouped by the dominant failure class carried ON the incident object (dominantClass on the src=incident open line). Distinct from 'Failures by class & severity' above, which counts step_failure events regardless of whether they formed an incident -- this counts the incidents themselves. Sorted by count. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: zot /v2/ liveness
panels.description: Whether the registry cache on the proxy VM answers GET /v2/ -- the check every guest-side gate performs before a pull. Green 'up' when it does, red 'DOWN' when it does not, 'n/a' when the probe has not run. Green here, with every other guest still present in the per-client panels below, means a guest that blamed the caching proxy lost its own path to the lab, not the proxy. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Guest pull path
panels.description: The pull a guest actually makes -- a manifest GET through the cache's ns= path -- judged by the deadline a real client applies. Green 'ok' when a pull started now would succeed; red 'FAILING' when a client would have abandoned it, whether the cache answered late or not at all. 'n/a' when the probe has not run. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Manifest path
panels.description: The canary manifest HEAD against the cache, judged by the same client deadline. Red here beside a green liveness tile is the signature of a sync stall: /v2/ answers in milliseconds while every pull times out, so a guest reports the proxy as unreachable although the endpoint is up. 'n/a' when the probe has not run. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Docker Hub budget
panels.description: Pulls left in the current Docker Hub window for the proxy's egress address, shared by every guest behind it. Green at 25 or more, amber from 10, red below. Exhaustion never reaches a guest as a clean 429 -- the guest sees a cache that stopped answering in time. 'n/a' when the budget could not be read, deliberately not painted as zero: the value is gated on the probe gauge. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: zot requests per client, per minute
panels.description: Every request the registry cache served, counted per minute and split by the address it came from; the source port is stripped so one guest is one line. This is the cache's own account of who it was talking to. A line that stops while the others carry on, under a green liveness tile, is a guest that lost its path to the lab -- the cache never saw it leave. 127.0.0.1 is the proxy VM's own probe. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

targets.expr: sum by (client) (count_over_time({job="zot"} | json | message="HTTP API" | label_format client=`{{ regexReplaceAll ":[0-9]+$" .clientIP "" }}` [1m]))

panels.title: squid requests per client, per minute
panels.description: Every request the web cache served, counted per minute and split by client address, from squid's own access log: the third field of each line is the client. Read it with the zot panel beside it -- a guest fetches packages through squid and images through zot, so a guest missing from both in the failing minute never reached the proxy VM at all, while a guest present here and absent from zot had a registry problem, not a network one. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Step failures that name the caching proxy
panels.description: The step_failure events whose reason or console tail mentions the caching proxy -- the place to start when a cycle blames the cache. Read each line against the tiles above and the per-client panels: a failure logged while liveness and the pull path were green, and while the other guests' lines carried on, is a guest that lost its own path to the lab, not a proxy outage. Expand a line for the host, the cycle and the console text that named the proxy. Details: Hosts dashboard guide.

panels.title: Available memory per host
panels.description: Physical memory available on each current pool host: Windows available bytes, Ubuntu MemAvailable, and a macOS estimate of free plus inactive pages. Minimum and Latest summarize the selected window; the sparkline preserves its history. Every current host is listed; n/a means no reading, not zero. Exporter reports scrape health at the window end: Up, Down, or Not scraped. A historical reading may remain when the exporter is now Down. Host ID opens the same full-ID and status-page menu as Pool hosts.

targets.expr: topk(1, yuruna_pool_host_info{pool=~"$pool"}) by (hostId) unless on(hostId) yuruna_pool_host_retired

panels.title: Commit headroom per host
panels.description: Commit limit minus committed bytes for Windows and Ubuntu. Windows measures memory it can still promise; Ubuntu reports CommitLimit minus Committed_AS, whose allocation meaning depends on the kernel overcommit policy and can be negative. Support identifies Windows and Ubuntu as Supported, macOS as Unsupported, and unrecognized platforms as Unknown. macOS has no equivalent commit counter, so its byte readings stay n/a even when Exporter is Up. Minimum and Latest summarize the selected window; the sparkline preserves its history. Every current host is listed; n/a means no reading, not zero; Support distinguishes an unsupported platform from a supported host with missing telemetry. Exporter reports scrape health at the window end: Up, Down, or Not scraped. A historical reading may remain when the exporter is now Down. Host ID opens the same full-ID and status-page menu as Pool hosts.
